scope: Targeted disposition of the existing 26 materials and known first-party acceptance boundaries. Not a complete current source-expression, contribution-rights or product SBOM audit. No license, NOTICE, original source register, review, golden or held evidence is changed.

legalAndScopeRules.rule: Project-owned source can adopt MIT only for a substantiated owned/licensable scope. Separately licensed dependencies, assets and copied portions keep their own licenses and notices; their being non-MIT is not itself a blocker for first-party MIT.

MIT permits publication/distribution with its copyright and permission notice retained. A package license identifier or unrelated release notice does not establish the missing original notice for a selected version.

Apache-2.0 section 4 allows different terms on one's modifications or a derivative as a whole while the Apache conditions on upstream material continue: license copy, changed-file notices, applicable attribution and NOTICE. Section 5 contribution defaults/separate agreements must be considered for actual contributions. No upstream grant is erased or whole-file independent authorship inferred.

Observed source exposure is not automatic disqualification from original expression. The current evidence still lacks acceptance for the named candidates, so neither clean-room claims nor global MIT grants follow. Technical passing checks prove a different fact.

Any-license-choice HOLD means release readiness has not been established for an artifact containing the unresolved component, not a finding of infringement or a prohibition on all possible separately scoped source publications. Existing public Git history is not relabeled unpublished.
